A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HalluGuard work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and recovering content affected by a localized layout overlap in v1.

before.justification: V1 reports original hallucination-detection benchmarks, score-guided inference results, ablations, runtime measurements, and synthetic diagnostic experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds encoder ablations and detection results on Snowballing, POPE, GovReport, and NarrativeQA.

M1.justification: The HalluGuard score in Equation 7, projection calibration, feature clipping, and score-guided inference procedure remain unchanged. The revised mean-response formulation changes the theoretical analysis; alternative encoders are tested as ablations rather than adopted into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.10 adds reported multimodal evaluation on POPE and long-context benchmark evaluation on GovReport and NarrativeQA, substantially expanding represented inputs and tasks. V1 already contained a long-document case study and Snowballing-based depth analyses; those are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds BERT-, SimCSE-, and E5-based comparison variants in the encoder ablation (Table 7). Existing detector rosters remain unchanged, including SAPLMA, LLM-Check, and ITI, which already appeared in v1 Table 7. The added benchmark tables reuse existing detectors.

E3.justification: V2 adds Pearson R and MSE measurements for the stability ablation, controlled encoder substitutions across five backbones and three benchmarks, and direct AUROC/AUPRC evaluation on Snowballing. Appendix C.1's default sampling, optimization, regularization, and beam-search settings are unchanged. Task-specific protocols for the new multimodal and long-context evaluations are not detailed.

E4.justification: The new encoder-sensitivity study in C.3 tests a previously unexamined explanation for HalluGuard's performance by replacing its representation with BERT, SimCSE, and E5 across several backbones and task families. C.2 also adds quantitative agreement/error measurements to the existing stability-term ablation. Earlier diagnostic plots and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify a fixed default seed and mean±standard deviation over five seeds for ablations in C.1. No new uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run procedures are reported. The added Pearson R and MSE entries are diagnostic point measurements.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 retain their values, but v1 Table 6 becomes v2 Table 8 with numerous lower HalluGuard scores and no stated protocol revision. GPT-2/RAGTruth F1 changes from 81.22 to 71.22; QwQ-32B/BBH F1 changes from 82.55 to 78.55, now below Inside's unchanged 79.17. V2 also adds substantial encoder-ablation and Snowballing, POPE, GovReport, and NarrativeQA results.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 redefine the perturbation map from an individual decoded representation to its expectation and revise the smoothness assumptions accordingly. Appendix A rewrites the projection/concentration argument and explicitly states a probability qualification. Theorem B.3 changes the inverse-determinant bound C_d det(K)^(-c_d)||u*|| to R_s det(K)^(s/r), with a different proof and constants; Section 3.3 nevertheless retains the inverse-power formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit open-source release contribution. The central claims about unified risk decomposition, NTK-based detection, and state-of-the-art performance remain unchanged, as do the headline claims of ten benchmarks, eleven baselines, and nine backbones.

C2.justification: C.3 newly interprets encoder-ablation results as evidence that gains arise from reasoning-trajectory geometry rather than surface semantic similarity. C.10 additionally interprets the new evaluations as robustness to multimodal noise and long-range dependency drift. Appendix A clarifies that smoothness concerns the expected semantic response rather than discrete decoding itself.

D1.justification: V2 newly announces model open-sourcing and supplies a HalluGuard repository hyperlink in the abstract and introduction. The detailed implementation and hyperparameter information in C.1 is unchanged. The new benchmark tables do not provide corresponding image-processing or long-context handling instructions.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for POPE, GovReport, NarrativeQA, and Ke et al. (2025). New C.9 explicitly distinguishes HalluGuard's structured risk decomposition from Inside and MIND's empirical uncertainty diagnostics. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the problem definition, assumption explanations, and proof exposition. V2 introduces a Given/Find problem statement, folds former A.3 into A.2, adds acknowledgements, and edits citation and affiliation presentation. The overall main-text organization and experimental narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds dedicated tables for stability diagnostics, encoder substitutions, Snowballing, and three additional benchmarks, substantially expanding the appendix's evidence displays. Repositioning Figure 2 and Table 3 removes their overlap in v1. All fourteen existing figure images are retained, while tables and surrounding text are reflowed; the SAPLMA/LLM-Check/ITI table also consolidates repeated dataset labels.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful encoder controls, clearer expectation-level assumptions, a source-access link, and a layout correction. However, revised Theorem B.3 conflicts with Section 3.3's retained inverse-determinant bound, and revised RAGTruth results in Table 8 conflict with Table 9—for example, GPT-2 F1 is 71.22 versus 81.22. The new multimodal and long-context results also lack task-specific processing details. These benefits and consistency problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
